name: XSS Prevention
description: Enforces output sanitization, Content Security Policy, and safe rendering patterns to prevent cross-site scripting.
content:
# XSS Prevention Rules

- Always encode output for the correct context — HTML entities for HTML, JavaScript encoding for inline scripts, URL encoding for URLs
- Use framework auto-escaping — React JSX, Angular template binding, and Vue mustache syntax all escape by default
- Never use unsafe innerHTML APIs with user-provided content — always sanitize with DOMPurify or similar libraries first
- Set a strict Content-Security-Policy header — at minimum `default-src 'self'`, avoid `unsafe-inline` and `unsafe-eval`
- Use CSP nonces or hashes for inline scripts — `script-src 'nonce-{random}'` instead of `'unsafe-inline'`
- Sanitize HTML when rich text is required — use DOMPurify, sanitize-html, or Bleach with an explicit allowlist of tags and attributes
- Set `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff` to prevent MIME type sniffing attacks
- Set `HttpOnly` flag on session cookies — prevents JavaScript from reading authentication cookies
- Validate URLs before rendering in `href` or `src` attributes — block `javascript:` and `data:` protocols
- Use Trusted Types API in modern browsers to enforce safe DOM manipulation — prevents DOM-based XSS
- Escape user input in JSON embedded in HTML — use JSON.stringify and HTML-encode the result
- Review third-party scripts for XSS risks — load external scripts with `integrity` (SRI) and `crossorigin` attributes
